title: Amazon Secures $80B Loan Facility to Fund AI Infrastructure
summary: Amazon establishes an $80 billion secured loan facility against hardware purchases to finance its massive AI data center expansion starting in 2027.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Amazon established an $80 billion secured loan facility against hardware purchases to preserve financial flexibility for AI investments.
- The facility is available from early 2027 through Q3 2028, marking Amazon's shift toward creative financing for data centers.
- Amazon's total spending commitments surged to $883 billion by September 2026, more than double the year-earlier figure.


Amazon has arranged a secured loan facility worth up to $80 billion against the value of hardware purchases, providing the company with new financial flexibility as it ramps up spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. The facility, disclosed in Amazon's quarterly filing on October 30, 2026, marks a strategic shift in how the e-commerce and cloud giant funds its AI ambitions.


## Structure and Timeline


Officially launched on October 30, 2026, the secured loan facility gives Amazon access to funds from the beginning of 2027 through the third quarter of 2028. Lenders receive collateral rights over assets purchased in connection with the facility, though Amazon's filing does not specify which hardware categories are included. The arrangement allows Amazon to tap the credit line at its discretion as capital needs arise.


Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman explained the rationale in a Bloomberg Television interview: "When we see such a really large opportunity in front of us, we're looking for ways to also responsibly fund that so that we can go as big as possible for our customers." The company is working with partners to balance cash flows during an aggressive infrastructure ramp-up period.


## Capital Spending Surge


Amazon reported larger-than-expected capital expenditures in its third quarter 2026 earnings, leading to a free cash outflow of $42.4 billion for the year ended September 30, 2026. Total spending commitments ballooned to $883 billion by the end of September, up 36% from three months earlier and more than double the figure from September 2025. The shares declined approximately 2% following the disclosure.


The secured loan facility represents Amazon's first major move toward creative financing arrangements for AI infrastructure. Until now, the company had funded data center construction and chip purchases primarily through cash from its cloud computing and retail operations, supplemented by corporate bond sales. This approach contrasts with rivals who have pursued joint ventures with investment groups or leased Nvidia chips purchased by third parties.


## Industry Context


Many technology companies have turned to alternative financing structures to manage the enormous capital requirements of AI infrastructure. Nvidia chips, which power most AI workloads, often represent the single most expensive component of new data center construction. Amazon's supplier financing arrangement provides a path to acquire these critical components while preserving balance sheet flexibility.


The facility's focus on hardware collateral suggests Amazon is securing access to servers, networking equipment, and potentially AI accelerators needed for expanding its AWS cloud infrastructure. By borrowing against the value of these purchases rather than traditional unsecured debt, Amazon can potentially secure more favorable terms while maintaining operational control over its buildout timeline.


## What This Means


Amazon's $80 billion secured loan facility signals that even the most cash-rich technology companies are exploring innovative capital structures to sustain AI investment levels. The arrangement provides Amazon with dry powder to compete in the infrastructure arms race while managing near-term cash flow pressures. As cloud providers race to build capacity for enterprise AI workloads, expect more creative financing solutions to emerge across the industry. The facility's 2027-2028 window aligns with the peak period of hyperscaler data center expansion, positioning Amazon to maintain its competitive stance in the cloud AI market.
